contentText:
Syllabus (GS3): Capital markets - securities, debt/bond instruments (short & long term), special-purpose bonds, electoral bonds.

1. Capital & Securities

Capital: Fixed capital = land/plant/machinery/furniture; Working capital = raw materials, salaries, rent, day-to-day operations. Retained earnings = profit re-invested in the business (rest paid as dividend; board decides the split).

Q - Equity (share) vs Debt (bond)?







Equity / Share



Debt / Bond (Debenture)





Holder gets dividend only if there is profit



Holder gets fixed interest + principal regardless of profit





Owner of the company



Creditor (lender) to the company





Last (residual) claim on liquidation



First claim on liquidation





Attractive in a boom (higher dividend potential)



Attractive in a slowdown (fixed, lower risk)

2. Financial / Securities Market - Types





By tenure: Money market (< 1 yr maturity) vs Capital market (>= 1 yr).



By freshness: Primary market (new securities issued first time; no physical location) vs Secondary market (resale of old securities, e.g. BSE Dalal Street) - resale liquidity encourages primary buying.



By settlement: Future market (contract now, deliver on a future date) vs Spot market (immediate delivery).



By asset: bond, share, G-Sec, forex, commodity markets. A single 'Universal Exchange' (all assets) was permitted for BSE & NSE (2018).

3. Short-Term Debt Instruments (< 1 year)

Traded in the money market; usually unsecured; sold at a discount and repurchased at face value (the gap = interest). Highly liquid = called 'Near Money'; negotiable & transferable.







Instrument



Issuer / meaning





Treasury Bills (14/91/182/364 days)



Union Govt only (States stopped since 2001); issued at a discount.





Cash Management Bill (91 days)



Union Govt, for temporary cash mismatch.





WMA / Overdraft / SDF



RBI's short-term (3-month) loans to Govts. WMA = at Repo%; Overdraft = Repo + 2-5%; not counted in fiscal deficit.





Certificate of Deposit (CD)



Unsecured negotiable debt issued by commercial banks.





Commercial Paper / Bill of Exchange / Hundi / Promissory Note



Issued by companies.





Call / Notice Money



Interbank borrowing for 1 day / 2-14 days.





CBLO



Collateralized Borrowing & Lending Obligation via Clearing Corp of India (money-market instrument).





Inter Corporate Deposit (ICD)



Unsecured short loan from one company to another.

Tri-Party Repo: adds a Tri-Party Agent (NSE/BSE) between borrower & lender for collateral custody; NOT a monetary-policy tool.

Q - Factoring & TReDS?





Factoring: an MSME pledges an unpaid invoice to a factor (bank/NBFC) for a short loan. Factoring Regulation (Amendment) Act 2021 opened it to all NBFCs (9000+) and requires invoice registration on the SARFAESI central registry (stops 'dual financing' fraud).



Bill discounting vs factoring: in bill discounting the MSME collects from the buyer and pays the factor; in factoring the factor collects directly from the buyer.



TReDS: online platform (M1xchange, RXIL, A.TReDS) linking factors with MSME borrowers; RXIL is owned by SIDBI + NSE.

Interest-rate benchmarks: LIBOR (London interbank rate), MIBOR (Mumbai). Post-LIBOR, RBI's Ramanathan Subramanian Committee proposed SORR (Secured Overnight Rupee Rate) (2024), computed by FBIL, may replace MIBOR.

4. Long-Term Debt Instruments (>= 1 year)





Colonial-era types: Coupon bonds (detachable coupons -> 'coupon rate'); Zero-coupon bonds (sold at discount, no coupon); Bearer bonds (not linked to ID; anyone holding gets paid; issued in war).



Modern Govt borrowing: G-Sec, dated securities, sovereign bonds - also called Gilt-edged securities (repayment assured -> lower interest).



Credit rating: AAA best (US Treasury); India ~BAA (moderate). Big-3 = Fitch, Moody's, S&P (critics: pro-US/EU bias).



Global bond indices: Indian G-Sec added to JPMorgan GBI-EM (2024) and Bloomberg EM Index (2025) -> more foreign inflows & liquidity.

Q - Special govt/RBI bonds?







Bond



Detail





Inflation Indexed Bond (IIB)



Gives positive real interest; RBI issued 1997/2004/2013/2018.





Capital Indexed Bond (CIB) vs IIB



CIB-1997 protected only principal (WPI); IIB-2013/IINSS-C protect principal + interest (IINSS-C uses CPI).





Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB, 2015)



RBI issues on Govt's behalf; denominated in gold grams but pays rupee value of gold at maturity (8 yr) + 2.5% interest; reduces physical gold import. 2025: Govt may stop (gold price ~doubled 2019->2024).

5. Company Long-Term Debt & Hybrids





Bond (British) = Debenture (American). Junk bonds = high default risk (BB-D, e.g. IL&FS) -> must offer high interest.



Redeemable (interest + principal returned) vs Irredeemable (only interest, no principal - e.g. PSB AT1 bonds).



Secured vs Unsecured; Convertible vs Non-convertible (NCD). Hybrid = issued as bond, convertible to share.



Mezzanine/Hybrid financing: debt + equity mix via OFCD (Optionally Fully Convertible Debentures); used by venture capitalists in start-ups; pays less interest than plain bonds.



FCCB: Foreign Currency Convertible Bond - foreign-currency bond convertible to shares at a pre-set rate; lower interest (conversion is the sweetener).



CoCo / Enhanced Capital Note: hybrid of AT1 bond + OFCD - converts to shares (or writes off) on a trigger condition.



Sahara OFCD: issued without SEBI nod -> SEBI penalty; CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal (2023) refunds investors.

6. Bonds by Issuer





Municipal (ULB) bonds: Ahmedabad = 1st municipal bond (1996); Lucknow = 1st from North India (2020); Ghaziabad = 1st green municipal bond (2021, private placement); Indore = 1st green muni bond for retail investors (2023).



Global: BRICS/New Development Bank bonds (USD); World Bank 'Bond-i' (2018, 1st blockchain bond, Australia); Evergrande (Chinese realty) bond crisis.

Q - Currency-named bonds?







Bond name



Borrowed in that country/currency





Masala Bond



Rupee-denominated bond issued OUTSIDE India (for Indian entities); IFC launched it; Kerala's KIIFB = 1st Indian state (2019).





Maharaja Bond



Rupee bond issued by a non-Indian INSIDE India.





Panda / Dim sum Bond



Yuan (Renminbi) bond in China / Hong Kong.





Kangaroo Bond



Australian-dollar bond in Australia (e.g. World Bank Bond-i).





Formosa Bond



Non-Taiwan-dollar bond issued in Taiwan.

Surety Bonds: allowed from Budget-2022, regulated by IRDAI (replace bank guarantees for contractors).

7. Special-Purpose Bonds





Green Bonds: for renewable energy/pollution control. World's 1st = World Bank (2007); India's 1st = Yes Bank (2015); IREDA's Masala green bond (2018); Sovereign Green Bonds (Budget-2022, via RBI E-Kuber). Fund NOT for nuclear/large hydro (>25MW)/tobacco etc.



Greenium: lower interest investors accept for green impact. ES24: Indian sovereign green bonds got little greenium; Jan-2025 issue ~70% unsold (trust/transparency, low liquidity, no big backer).



Blue Bond: green sub-type for marine/fisheries (Seychelles, 2018, 1st). ESG Bonds: issued by firms strong on Environment/Social/Governance.



Consol / Perpetual bonds: no maturity, pay interest forever (irredeemable); some propose Consol bonds for post-Covid revival.



Elephant Bonds (proposed): 25-yr bonds where black-money declarers invest, funds for infrastructure. Sukuk: sharia-compliant (Islamic) bond.



Social/Skill Impact Bonds: SIDBI Women's Livelihood Bonds (2019, 3% for 5 yr, for women entrepreneurs); NSDC Skill Impact Bond (2021).



CAT (Catastrophe) Bonds: for disaster risk. Bhutan 'Nation Building Bond' ($100M) for Gelephu Mindfulness City.



Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP): by NPO/NGO; repays NEITHER interest NOR principal; like a donation but with SEBI disclosure; traded on the Social Stock Exchange (e.g. Unnati, 2023).

8. Electoral Bonds

Electoral Bonds (Budget-2017): issued only by SBI (in Rs.1k to Rs.1cr denominations); bought by Indian citizens/companies (with KYC, not cash/anonymous); donated to parties (registered under RPA 1951 with >=1% votes); 15-day validity; paper bearer promissory note, interest-free, non-transferable.





SC ban (Feb-2024): electoral bonds violate voters' right to know (Art 19(1)(a)), RPA, Companies Act & IT Act; donor privacy < voters' right to know. SBI must disclose all donors & recipient parties (2019-24) to ECI.



Companies Act (2017 amendment struck down): had removed the 7.5%-of-3-yr-avg-profit donation cap and the need to name the recipient party - SC ruled it unconstitutional (2024).



Electoral Trusts (2013): a company creates a trust that pools donations and distributes to parties (donor anonymity); NOT banned.

9. Misc Bonds & Repayment Buffers





Market-Linked Debentures: interest linked to an index (Sensex, G-Sec yield, gold).



Debenture Redemption Reserve (DRR): buffer fund a company keeps (Companies Act) to repay bondholders; some firms exempted (2019).



Consolidated Sinking Fund (CSF): buffer fund for State Govts' loan repayment.

Key Facts (Quick Revision)







Fact



Detail





Equity vs Debt



Shareholder = owner, last claim; Bondholder = lender, first claim.





Money vs Capital market



< 1 yr vs >= 1 yr maturity.





Near Money



Highly liquid: T-Bill, savings a/c, money-market instruments.





Gilt-edged



Govt securities (assured repayment).





SGB (2015)



Gold-gram denominated; pays rupee value of gold at maturity + 2.5%.





Masala Bond



Rupee bond issued outside India; IFC; Kerala KIIFB (1st state).





Sovereign Green Bond



Budget-2022; via RBI E-Kuber; not for nuclear/large-hydro.





Electoral Bonds



Budget-2017; only SBI; banned by SC (Feb-2024).
